To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the superconducting transition of a 2D electron gas is of second order and belongs to the universality class of 3D XY transitions; (ii) the superconductivity is destroyed by the formation of a vortex lattice, which is a signature of a 2nd-order transition; (iii) the critical temperature is determined by a single energy scale, which can be extracted from the temperature dependence of the critical magnetic field.
the density driven superconducting transition of a two dimensional system is a continuous transition, and it belongs to the same universality class as the thermal transition.

the superfluid density is a good order parameter to describe the transition from a 2D superconductor to a normal metal, and that the superconducting transition in a 2D system is a QPT in the 2D XY universality class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects of the superconducting phase transition:   1.
the study of the fluctuation regime in a two-dimensional (2D) superconductor, in the vicinity of the superconductor-insulator transition (SIT), using a scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) setup.
the study of the quantum critical regime in a two-dimensional (2D) superconductor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transition from the ordered to the disordered phase in the two-dimensional superconductive system is a continuous one, and the universality class is that of the 2D XY model.
, in general, a QPT can be described in the framework of a quantum field theory.
the superfluid phase is a topological phase, which is characterized by a non-zero topological charge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to measure density fluctuations in a superconductor and that these fluctuations can be used to study the QPT in a two dimensional system.
the fluctuation regime of a QPT in a two-dimensional system, is the same as for a thermal phase transition.
the QPT of the two dimensional superconductor is of the Kosterlitz-Thouless type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluctuation regime of a two-dimensional superconducting transition is not universal, but it depends on the microscopic details of the system.
, for a QPT, the fluctuation regime is controlled by the density of states at the Fermi energy, which can vary significantly from material to material.
, in the presence of a density gradient, the fluctuation regime can be modified.
